sections.h2: How do I sell a house fast in Kingsport?
sections.html:
In Kingsport you can list the house, sell it to a buyer you find yourself, or accept a cash offer from someone who buys it as is. A cash sale is the shortest path when the house needs work or you are working against a date, such as a tax deadline or a move.

Kingsport is one of the Tri-Cities and spans two counties, Sullivan and Hawkins, so a few steps depend on where your parcel sits. The city bill, the county assessor and the register of deeds all vary by county.

  • Listing suits houses that show well and owners who can wait on a buyer's loan.
  • A private sale needs a closing agent and a clean deed.
  • A cash purchase can close on a date you set, with repairs left to the buyer.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Kingsport?
sections.html:
Kingsport sits on the Holston River at the northwest end of Interstate 26, where U.S. 11W and U.S. 23 cross. The city limits reach west into Hawkins County and north to the Virginia line. Its name is a shortening of King's Port, after King's Boat Yard, once the head of navigation for the Tennessee Valley. It was chartered in 1822 and rechartered in 1917, when it was rebuilt as a garden city with a plan by John Nolen, which earned it the nickname Model City.

Eastman Chemical Company has its headquarters and first chemical plant here. Domtar runs a recycled containerboard mill that dates to a 1916 paper mill, and the Holston Army Ammunition Plant makes explosives for the Department of Defense. Two Ballad Health hospitals, Holston Valley Medical Center and Indian Path Community Hospital, serve the city, and the Kingsport Academic Village downtown hosts Lincoln Memorial University and Northeast State.

Almost all residents are in Kingsport City Schools, which operates eight elementary schools, two middle schools (Ross N. Robinson and John Sevier) and Dobyns-Bennett High School. The Kingsport Area Transit Service runs four bus routes. Neighborhood names buyers search include Lynn Garden, Colonial Heights, Rock Springs, Bloomingdale and Cliffside.

sections.h2: How do Kingsport's Census figures compare for housing?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimates Kingsport had 57,530 residents on July 1, 2025, up 3.6 percent from April 2020. About 23.3 percent are 65 or older, and 20.6 percent are under 18.

  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 60.1 percent
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $234,100
  • Median monthly owner cost with a mortgage: $1,387
  • Median gross rent: $907
  • Median household income: $52,490
  • Households: 25,021

Kingsport's land area is 52.6 square miles, with a density of about 1,054 people per square mile.

sections.h2: What does the local economy mean for Kingsport buyers?
sections.html:
Manufacturing anchors the city. Wikipedia reports a 2019 gross metropolitan product of $14.1 billion for the Kingsport area, and the Census Bureau's 2022 business tallies show $1.96 billion in retail sales and $1.25 billion in health care and social assistance receipts for the city.

Only 54.6 percent of residents aged 16 and over are in the civilian labor force, and the mean commute is 19.1 minutes. A shorter drive is a point in favor of listing in town rather than farther out in either county. If your house is near the Eastman complex, the Kingsport Academic Village downtown, or the Holston Valley hospital campus, say so in the listing or when you describe the house to a cash buyer.

Kingsport also has neighborhoods with different histories. Downtown, Riverfront and Midtown sit near the original plan, while Colonial Heights and Preston Forest are outlying areas the city names among its neighborhoods.

sections.h2: When are Kingsport city property taxes due and what are the penalties?
sections.html:
The City of Kingsport bills its own property tax. The 2026 bills were due on or before November 30, 2026, and that date is still ahead in mid-November 2026, so a house that closes before then should have the bill settled at closing. Unpaid balances pick up penalties on a fixed schedule that city officials cannot waive.

DatePenalty added to unpaid city tax
December 1, 20262%
January 1, 2027Another 2%
First of each later monthAnother 1% until paid

Source: City of Kingsport property tax notice for 2026. Pay online by eCheck with no added fee, by card with a 2.75 percent fee, by mail, or at the Customer Service Center at 415 Broad Street. Property tax cannot be paid by phone. For help call 423-343-9860.

The city's page lists a 2025 tax rate of $1.67 per $100 and a 2024 rate of $1.99. It also notes that Sullivan County reassessed in 2025, after the previous reassessment in 2021.

sections.h2: Which county assessor do I call about a Kingsport house?
sections.html:
Call the assessor in the county where the parcel sits, because the city bill depends on county assessments. For a Sullivan County parcel, the Assessor of Property is at 3411 Highway 126 in Blountville, 423-323-6455. For a Hawkins County parcel, the office is at 110 East Main Street in Rogersville, 423-272-8505.

Residential property is assessed at 25 percent of value under state law. Tennessee also runs a property tax relief program for homeowners who are 65 or older or disabled. For the 2026 bills, the city lists a cap of $38,470 on 2025 income and the value used in the calculation at $33,600, while a 100 percent service-connected disabled veteran or surviving spouse has a $175,000 value limit with no income test. Kingsport adds a city rebate of up to $40 for people who qualify. Details are on the state comptroller's tax relief site, and the state phone line is 615-747-8871.

An owner who moved should update the mailing address with the county assessor, since the city says not receiving a notice or disputing a value does not excuse a late payment.

sections.h2: Where is a deed recorded and what does the state charge?
sections.html:
For a house in Sullivan County, the Register of Deeds is at 3411 Highway 126, Suite 101, in Blountville, phone 423-323-6420, open 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays. Tennessee charges a realty transfer tax of $0.37 per $100 of price, so a sale at the Census median value of $234,100 carries about $866 in transfer tax. A mortgage tax of $0.115 per $100 of debt applies to the buyer's new loan after the first $2,000.

Who pays the transfer tax is negotiated in the contract. If part of your lot or house lies in Hawkins County, ask the title company which register records the deed before you set a closing date.

sections.h2: What permits does Kingsport require before I sell or rent the house?
sections.html:
Kingsport requires permits for most renovation work, including roofs, decks, porches, additions, finishing a basement, new electrical or plumbing, water heater replacement and furnace installation. Cosmetic work like paint, cabinets and floor coverings does not need one, and fences do not. A homeowner who lives in the house may buy permits when doing the work personally, after filing a Homeowner's Affidavit.

Owners of rental property may do cosmetic repairs themselves, but electrical, plumbing and mechanical permits require a licensed contractor. Contractors on jobs under $25,000 need the city business license, and jobs over that amount need a State of Tennessee contractor's license. The Building Division can be reached at 423-229-9393. Permits can be paid for online through the city portal, though not by phone.

faqs.q: When is Kingsport city property tax due?
faqs.a: November 30 each year. For 2026 it is November 30, 2026, then 2 percent is added on December 1 and another 2 percent on January 1, followed by 1 percent each month.

faqs.q: Does Kingsport have property tax relief for seniors?
faqs.a: Yes. The state program covers homeowners 65 or older or disabled within income limits, and Kingsport adds a city rebate of up to $40. The 2026 income cap listed by the city is $38,470.

faqs.q: Which county is my Kingsport house in?
faqs.a: Most of Kingsport is in Sullivan County, and a western portion is in Hawkins County. The city's tax lookup asks you to select the county, and the assessor for that county handles value and address questions.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer tax on a Kingsport home sale?
faqs.a: The state rate is $0.37 per $100 of purchase price. A $234,100 sale would owe about $866, and the contract says who pays it.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to replace a water heater in Kingsport?
faqs.a: Yes. Kingsport lists installing or replacing hot water heaters among the work that needs a plumbing permit. Fences and cosmetic updates do not need permits.
